ideas.description: Re-validate a feasible commit that was discarded only for its timing. E071 (commit 5769443: E069 plus freezing block 2's first conv for the last 10% of samples) scored 0.7551 on seeds 0-2, which is feasible, at 4.636 s versus E069's 4.678 s (-0.9%). It was discarded under the '<1% is jitter' contingency, but the saving is a deterministic FLOP cut (one wgrad plus one NS group on ~22 steps). Gate offline in drafts/, untimed: on a quiet host (check that no other job is on the box with nvidia-smi), run E069 and E071 through the benchmark build/prepare/train path as interleaved processes A,B,A,B,A,B, 3 trials each, with the Inductor cache warm. Log per-trial train time and host load. If the paired mean train-time gap is >=0.5% (about 23 ms) in E071's favour and per-seed accuracy on seeds 0-2 matches E071's logged values to within 0.02 pp, launch commit 5769443 unchanged as the experiment. Confirm the build stays under 600 s (it was 424 s). No code changes.
ideas.expected: Accuracy 0.7551, identical per seed to E071 because the run is deterministic (see the E003/E038 reproducibility). Time 4.62-4.66 s, point ~4.64 s (-0.8% vs 4.678). That is feasible and faster, so it becomes a new best. If the offline paired gap is <0.3%, E071's -0.9% was jitter: do not launch, and close H7.3.

ideas.description: Math-preserving CUDA-graph capture of the low-res train steps. E050 showed small maps are latency-bound (20->16 px saved 0.8% instead of the ~2% FLOP estimate). E038's finding that launch overhead is hidden was measured at 32 px, where steps are ~2.5x heavier. Gate first in drafts/ on the tip: for 20 steps each of the 20 px, 28 px and 32 px train graphs, compare the cuda-event wall time per step with the summed kernel time from the profiler. Launch only if the idle/launch gap in the 20 px plus 28 px stages totals >=0.05 s per trial (~1%). If it does, make one change: run the full-batch 20 px graph (with and without whitening-bias grad) and the full-batch 28 px graph under CUDA graphs. Use Inductor cudagraph trees (mode='max-autotune' for those variants only) and check the logs for 'skipping cudagraphs' caused by BN running-stat mutation. If they are skipped, fall back to a manual torch.cuda.CUDAGraph capture of forward+backward, following E038's pattern: static input buffer filled with copy_, grads with set_to_none=False, and parameters/buffers that prepare() resets IN PLACE so addresses stay valid across trials. Straddling partial-batch steps and all 32 px steps stay as they are. Record/capture every graph in build() on synthetic channels_last tensors. Compare trial-0 with later-trial train times. Base: the I101 successor if kept, else E069.
ideas.expected: Accuracy identical to the base per seed (within 0.02 pp), because the kernels and the RNG stream are unchanged. Time -1% to -3%, point -1.5% (~4.57-4.61 s): ~115 low-res steps lose ~0.5-1 ms of launch/gap time each. Keep if feasible and >=1% faster, since the saving is deterministic and pre-measured (the E051 precedent). If the gate shows <0.05 s of gap, retire without a run: low-res steps are GPU-latency-bound, not launch-bound.

ideas.description: Offline reproducibility check in drafts/; the submission is unchanged. Rerun E069 (5ed8687) on seeds 0-2 through the benchmark path in a fresh process with the Inductor cache intact. Compare per-seed accuracy with the logged E069 values. Also log per-trial prepare and train times, and the trial-0 vs trial-1/2 train excess. This is the precondition for the math-preserving cuts (I101, I102, fixed-overhead cleanup): they only keep the tip's seeds-0-2 score if a rerun of the same math reproduces it. Run it before I102 is launched.
ideas.expected: No metric change. Prediction: per-seed accuracy matches within 0.02 pp. That supports H4.1.7: math-preserving changes keep the 0.7561 draw, so systems cuts can be stacked safely. If any seed differs by >0.05 pp, cudnn.benchmark/max-autotune adds process-level nondeterminism. Every bit-identical cut then re-draws (~0.1-0.24 pp), so I101/I102 need a margin check before launch, and H4.1.1 loses E003's support. The per-trial time breakdown also sizes the fixed-overhead idea.

ideas.description: Fixed per-trial overhead cleanup, math-preserving. Gate on the per-trial breakdown from the H4.1.7 rerun (or E069's logs): prepare time per trial, and the trial-0 train excess over trials 1-2 (E040 saw ~0.06 s). Launch only if prepare plus the mean trial-0 excess is >=0.03 s (~0.6%). Then make one change, aimed at whichever is larger. (a) Trial-0 excess: warm up every timed path in build() with tensors of the exact shape, dtype and channels_last layout used in train(). This covers the per-epoch augment graphs (interpolate to 20/28 px, the low-res no-translate variant, jitter), the randperm/gather shapes and every straddle partial shape, plus the lookahead blend and both Muon variants. (b) Prepare: load the uint8 train array into pinned host memory and copy it with non_blocking=True, and drop any intermediate float/CPU copies. Keep the whitening-fit math, its input subset and its dtype bit-identical. Verify in drafts/ that seed-0 initial parameters, whitening weights and final per-seed accuracy are bit-identical to the base. Base: the current tip.
ideas.expected: Accuracy identical to the base per seed. Time -0.3% to -1.2%, point -0.6% (~0.03 s). Keep if feasible and faster with bit-identical accuracy: the saving is deterministic even though it is near jitter. Check the per-trial breakdown, not just the mean. If the gate shows <0.03 s of overhead, retire it: fixed overheads are already negligible.

ideas.description: Muon lr 0.16 -> 0.20 on the Polar Express base, scored on extra seeds first. Gate offline in drafts/: run E069 with only the Muon lr changed to 0.20 (0-d tensor, no recompile) on seeds 3-12, paired against the existing E069 seeds-3-12 results in drafts/extra_seeds (mean 0.75258). Launch the seeds-0-2 run only if the paired 10-seed gain is >=+0.12 pp (~1 paired sd). If it is kept, the banked margin goes straight to the block-1 freeze at 0.7 (E073 config, -0.11 pp paired, -2.2% time) as the next idea. E046 tested 0.20 only on NS3 at bs 1536 (-0.10 pp, seeds 0-2). PE spreads the same Frobenius norm over ~95% of directions instead of ~86%, so per-direction rotation is smaller and the optimum may have moved up. E075 (0.12: -0.89 pp) shows 0.16 is near the lower cliff.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±1%). On seeds 3-12, paired delta -0.2 to +0.3 pp, point +0.08 pp. A gain >=0.15 pp supports H1.2.8 and funds the freeze-at-0.7 cut (~-2.2%). Within ±0.1 pp: the plateau is flat on PE too, so close the Muon-lr axis. A drop >=0.3 pp means the upper cliff moved down under PE.

ideas.description: Averaging ramp, the first untested H1.6.1 candidate. Change only the lookahead blend ramp from (t/T)^3 to (t/T)^2. Base decay 0.97^5, sync every 5 steps and everything else stay the same. The decay is a Python float applied eagerly (I075), so nothing recompiles. Gate offline on seeds 3-12 paired against E069's existing results. Launch on seeds 0-2 only if the paired gain is >=+0.12 pp. Rationale: lookahead is worth ~1 pp (E008/E020), but only its horizon was ever tuned (E028, flat). A softer ramp brings averaging in earlier in the 32 px stage, where E025/E033 suggest diverse iterates feed the average. If kept, spend the margin on the freeze at 0.7.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Paired 10-seed delta -0.25 to +0.3 pp, point +0.05 pp. A gain >=0.15 pp supports H1.6.1, and EMA-on-top or sync-every-3 becomes the next arm. Within ±0.1 pp: the ramp is flat like the horizon, so close H1.6.1 and the averaging axis. A drop >=0.2 pp means early averaging drags the slow weights toward stale low-res iterates.

ideas.description: Explore matched-FLOP width reallocation between blocks 1 and 2 under Muon. On E069, change the block widths from 128/384 to 160/352 (block 3 stays 576). In drafts/, first compute per-step FLOPs at 20, 28 and 32 px. If the 160/352 split is not within ±1.5% of the tip's FLOPs, adjust block 2 in multiples of 32. Keep the Muon shape groups batched (160x1440 pair, 352x3168 pair, the new 160->352 first conv in its own group) and the frozen-block-1 variants consistent. Warm up every resolution and freeze variant plus their partial shapes in build() with channels_last tensors, keep the build under 600 s, and run debug_nan.py. Gate: score offline on seeds 3-12 paired against E069. Launch on seeds 0-2 only if the paired gain is >=+0.12 pp and offline train time is within +1%.
ideas.expected: Time within ±1.5% (FLOP-matched; E013 showed time tracks FLOPs). Paired 10-seed accuracy -0.4 to +0.35 pp, point 0.0. A gain >=0.15 pp supports H1.12 and opens a width axis (try 192/320 next). Within ±0.15 pp: the split is flat, so close H1.12. A drop >=0.25 pp means block-2 width is the scarcer capacity, consistent with E062 (block 2 still learning late).

Nothing is queued: every idea up to I100 is done or dropped. The tip is E069: 4.678 s, 0.7561 on seeds 0-2, but its 13-seed mean is about 0.7534, so a change that re-draws seeds 0-2 is roughly a coin flip at the 0.753 gate. The main exploit is therefore time cuts that preserve the math and keep each seed's result unchanged.

- **I101 (priority 5):** confirm with offline paired timing, then relaunch E071. That commit was already feasible (0.7551) and 0.9% faster, and was discarded only as possible jitter.
- **I102 (priority 4):** CUDA-graph the 20 px and 28 px train steps. E050 suggests these small-map stages are latency-bound. The idea is gated on a measured launch/idle gap.
- **H4.1.7 rerun (priority 4):** confirm that a rerun reproduces E069 per seed. The math-preserving cuts rely on this.
- **Fixed-overhead cleanup (priority 3):** remove the trial-0 first-call excess and cut prepare time, keeping everything bit-identical.

Explore (about 40%): Muon lr 0.20 on the Polar Express base (H1.2.8), a (t/T)^2 lookahead ramp (H1.6.1), and a matched-FLOP 160/352 width split (H1.12.1). All three are gated on paired results over seeds 3-12 against E069's existing extra-seed runs, because 3-seed deltas below ~0.4 pp are unreliable. Any real gain should fund the block-1 freeze at 0.7, which costs about 0.11 pp and saves about 2.2%.

Tree bookkeeping: the I075 gate already refutes H1.6.6, and the I098 paired result (-0.07 pp) refutes H1.2.9 and H1.2.7. The tree should be updated to match. Nothing was dropped because nothing was queued.
